restatements.text: Voids all city minimum wage ordinances and establishes that only the state can regulate the minimum wage.

findings.quote: Any city ordinance setting a minimum wage is void.
findings.mechanism: Eliminates city-level minimum wage rules, removing workers' ability to earn a locally set minimum wage that exceeds the state rate.

findings.quote: Any city ordinance setting a minimum wage is void.
findings.mechanism: Relieves employers from complying with and paying higher local minimum wages.

findings.direction: Shifts authority over minimum wage regulation from local governments to the state.
findings.quote: The state occupies the whole field of minimum wage regulation.
findings.mechanism: Preempts local authority by asserting exclusive state jurisdiction over minimum wage laws.

analysis.answer: Current law allows cities to establish their own minimum wage rates higher than the state's. This measure changes that by voiding all existing local minimum wage ordinances and granting the state exclusive authority over minimum wage regulation.

There is no direct budgetary cost to the state. The primary cost is borne by workers in cities with local minimum wages who will lose the wage premium over the state minimum. Cities may also lose administrative functions related to local wage enforcement.

Workers in cities that previously had higher minimum wages bear the cost in the form of lower mandated pay floors. Employers in those cities benefit from reduced wage minimums and the elimination of local compliance paperwork.

Employers may alter their hiring practices or pricing due to lower wage mandates. Workers might face increased financial strain in cities with high living costs. Advocacy efforts regarding the minimum wage will shift entirely from city councils to the state legislature.

The text addresses the problem of a regulatory patchwork where businesses operating in multiple cities face varying local wage laws. The mechanism achieves uniformity by overriding local rules. However, it removes the ability of localities to adjust wage floors to match local costs of living.
The state legislature gains exclusive power over minimum wage policy, while city councils and local voters lose their authority to regulate local wages.

The broader economic effects of minimum wage levels are heavily disputed. Some economic research finds that higher local minimum wages reduce employment or hours for low-wage workers, while other studies find no significant negative employment effects but note increased worker incomes and reduced poverty.

items.text: Reduces compliance burdens and labor cost floors for businesses by standardizing the minimum wage statewide.
Workers in cities lose the protection of local minimum wages that exceed the state rate.
Shifts authority over minimum wage regulation entirely from cities to the state.
Workers retain the ability to be protected by higher minimum wages set by their city.
Businesses forgo a simplified, single statewide minimum wage and the relief from higher local wage requirements.
